newsitem.title: USA: Europa Cruise to take $1.3mln charge in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Europa Cruise to take $1.3mln charge in Q2.

text.p: Europa Cruises Corp said Thursday it will take a $1.3 million one-time charge in the second quarter ending June 30.
The charge is part of an agreement the operator of casino boats reached with the Florida Department of Revenue to settle a $7.4 million assessment for $1.9 million, Europa said.
Europa said the settlement calls for monthly payments of $21,000 for seven years, with no interest for the first three years and 3-percent interest for the last 4 years.

The Florida Department of Revenue in November 1994 issued a notice of intent to make sales and use tax changes to Europa's return for the period February 1 1989 to June 15 1994. The proposed assessment including penalties and interest through June 15 totaled about $7.4 million, Europa said.

The company reported a net profit of $688,500, or $0.028 per share, for the quarter ended March 31, compared with a net loss of $171,500, or $0.01 per share, the year before. Europa's stock traded at 27/32 Thursday afternoon, up 1/16.
Company officials were not immediately available to elaborate on the settlement.
